decision_maker: Assistant Director of Planning (Chief Planning Officer)
purpose:
To appoint consultants to undertake a Retail
& Leisure Capacity Study in support of the emerging Mansfield
District Local Plan. This replaces the previous study completed in
early 2020.
content:
Mansfield District Retail &
Leisure Study 2026
 
Delegated Decision Ref:
26/06/PL
 
To
appoint suitably qualified and experienced consultants –
Lambert Smith Hampton (LSH) through the direct award route
to refresh and update the Leisure & Retail
evidence base required to support the development of Mansfield
District Council’s emerging Local Plan as it reaches the
regulation 19 Publication Stage. The expected price and contractor
along with the reasoning for a direct award are set out in the
contract exceptions form ref 64 attached to this Officer Decision
Record.
 
The Legal Services Manager be
authorised to negotiate, finalise and complete all necessary legal
agreements and other documents to give effect to the
above.

Regulation 19 stage of plan preparationunder the current plan making regulations provides that this
should be the Council’s final version of the Local Plan
before it is submitted to the Planning Inspectorate (PINS) acting
for the Secretary of State (regulation 22 stage) for an Examination
in Public (EIP).
 
The procurement of an up-to-date evidence base is an
essential part of preparing the Mansfield District Local Plan
review. The need for a retail study was identified in ODR
decision 25/10/SD (MR).
 
Much of the current retail
& Leisure evidence base for the district is now out of date and
requires updating to inform policies and site allocations within
the Local Plan Review.
 
In the case of Retail &
Leisure, the last study was completed in January 2020 with some of
the retail data sources stemming from 2017/18. This was pre-Brexit,
pre-Covid pandemic and pre changes in the Use Classes Order (Sept
2020) which provided for greater flexibility in respect of uses
predominantly found in Town Centres being allowed to change use
without the need for Planning Permission. In addition, both the
National Planning Policy Framework and National Planning Practice
Guidance has been updated since then.
 
Without an up-to-date
proportionate evidence base, the Council’s Local Plan would
be unlikely to be found sound at examination. The Council’s
Local Plan should seek to locate growth in the most sustainable
locations, and that the policies are justified. The evidence base
is needed to ensure that this can be demonstrated.
 
The government has made clear
that the transitional plan making arrangements under the Level Up
& Regeneration Act (LURA) will come to an end on the
31st December 2026. Plans prepared after that date will
need to follow a new plan making procedure. It is anticipated based
on advice from the Planning Advisory Service (PAS) that a
2-to-3-year delay could ensue should the deadline for submission by
31 December 2026 be missed and the new procedure followed. Such a
delay could cause a range of evidence collected to date to go out
of date with additional costs to then update. The Adopted Local
Plan 2013 - 2033 will also continue to lose relevance as it becomes
further out of date resulting in it losing weight in decision
making and decisions being made on a national policy basis rather
than at the local level.
 
In order to submit to PINS the
new emerging Mansfield Local Plan by 31st December 2026,
it has been identified that the Regulation 19 Publication version
of the plan would need to be published for consultation in late
September 2026 at the latest, with the Overview & Scrutiny
committee (1st September) and Full Council
(15th September) committee lead in times meaning the
local plan will need to be published as committee
papers  on the
25th  August 2026.
 
To meet such tight timescales,
it is estimated that the updated retail & leisure evidence is
needed by the end of June / early July to inform the revision of
and preparation of relevant leisure & retail policies to
complete the regulation19 plan ready for publication.
 
There has unfortunately been
unexpected delay in commissioning a new Retail & Leisure study
in the first part of 2026 due to the unexpected absence and then
loss of a temporary officer tasked with commissioning the retail
& leisure work. This was due to a change in their personal
circumstances.
 
As a consequence, it has become
clear that a direct award approach has now become necessary in
order for the retail & Leisure evidence to be collected in time
to meet the tight timescales referenced in the narrative above. A
contract exception approach due to urgency is supported by the
Assistant Director of Planning.

purpose:

content:
The Director of Corporate Resources/Deputy CEO
presented an overview of the report to the Committee.
 
Members were informed that the Accounting

Statement of Accounts.
 
The Committee was informed that officers had
reviewed the accounting policies to check that the policies were
clearly explained and underpinned the accounting transactions
within the Council’s Statement of Accounts for 2025/2026.
Following the review of the previous policies they were deemed to
be to the latest legislative compliance and that the accounting
policies were in accordance with the latest version of the code of
practice and IFRS requirements.
 
The Committee was informed that in respect of
2025/2026 there was one key change from 2024/2025 related to the
policy for depreciation. After reviewing the policy and seeking
advice from external advisors and the councils’ external
auditors it was recommended that the depreciation charge for
council dwellings be amended from 30 years to 50 years. The
recommendation was due to the investment in housing stock that had
taken place which had increased the longevity of the
properties.
 
The Committee was informed that as the
2025/2026 Statement of Accounts was being prepared that there may
need the need for additional amendments to the accounting policies
and if this were to be the case, this Committee would be informed
and the reason for this provided to the Committee.
 
Councillor Hughes proposed that the
recommendations be approved, Councillor Tempest Mitchell seconded
the motion.
 
On Putting the motion to the vote, it was
unanimously approved.
 
Resolved:
i)                   
That the 2025/2026 Accounting Policies be approved for use within
the Statement of Accounts.
ii)                 
That the Committee notes that further amendments may be required to
the policies as the accounts process progresses and these
amendments will be brought back to the next available meeting.

content:
The Corporate Assurance Manager presented an
overview of the Internal Audit Plan for April -June 2026 and

The Corporate Assurance Manager informed the
Committee that the proposed Internal Audit Plan for the period 1
April – 30 June 2026 at Table 1 had been presented for
approval by the Committee.
 
The Committee was presented with the
background of the report that detailed that Table 1 and 2 had been
compiled by the Corporate Assurance Manager in accordance with the
approved Internal Audit Charter to ensure compliance with the
Global Internal Audit Standards, and the plans had been compiled
with the agreed flexible planning approach. This approach the
Committee was informed allowed the Corporate Assurance Manager the
flexibility to prioritise works if special investigations were
required to be undertaken.
 
The Corporate Assurance Manager informed the
Committee that as at Table 1 a lot of work had been undertaken to
ensure that the Corporate Procurement arrangements were implemented
to ensure full compliance with the Council's Contract Procedure
Rules and Procurement Act 2023. Works had also been undertaken to
ensure that the delivery of the Internal Audit’s counter
fraud testing programme which was linked to the counter fraud
register would continue to be enforced.
 
The Corporate Assurance Manager informed the
Committee that there had been a significant improvement in the
procurement arrangements, in the overall process and arrangements
due to the procedures being more robust. This would continue to be
monitored to continue the assurance that the procurement and
counter fraud processes were being followed. The Officers would
continue to be challenged to ensure that the compliance register
would also be kept up to date.
 
 
The Corporate Assurance Manager advised the
Committee that only high and medium risks were audited.
 
Councillor Tempest Mitchell queried how risk
was calculated; and what was deemed to be a low risk.
 
The Corporate Assurance Manager informed the
Committee that the risk was based on several factors that included
cost and value. The factors were entered into the matrix and that
would indicate a red, amber, or green result.
 
Low risk factors were areas such as
environmental services, pest control, and dog control. However, it
an area of concern was raised by a service director this would be
audited.
 
The Corporate Assurance Manager advised that
how risk assessment took place was part of the training that had
been undertaken by the Committee.
 
The Committee was informed that the Internal
Audit Charter was a formal document that defined the internal
audit’s purpose, responsibility and position within the
organisation and the recommendation to the committee was that the
revised Internal Audit Charter be approved.
 
Councillor Denness proposed that the Internal
Audit Plan for the period for 1 April -30 June 2026 be approved;
and that the revised Internal Audit Plan be approved. Councillor
Hughes seconded the motion.
 
On putting the motion to the vote, it was
unanimously approved.
 
Resolved:
i)                   
That the Internal Audit Plan for the period 1 April 2026 – 30
June 2026 be approved.
ii)                 
That the revised Internal Audit Charter be approved.

content:
That
the Whole Plan Viability Assessment (WPVA) contract (to support the development of Mansfield District Council’s
emerging Local Plan Review) is awarded to the successful
contractor as detailed in the attached exempt appendix.
 
The
Legal Services Manager be authorised to negotiate, finalise and
complete all necessary legal agreements and other documents to give
effect to the above.
 
That
the budgets are amended to reflect the relevant expenditure.
The study is to be funded through an approved
reserve.
 

The procurement of an up-to-date evidence base is an
essential part of preparing the Mansfield District Local Plan
review.
 
Much of the current evidence
base for the district is out of date and requires updating to
inform policies and site allocations within the Local Plan Review.
In some cases, the guidance for the production of specific studies
has also changed alongside updates to the Planning Practice
Guidance[1] and National Planning Policy
Framework[2].
 
Without a satisfactory evidence
base the council’s Local Plan Review would be unlikely to be
found sound at examination. The council’s Local Plan Review
should seek to locate growth in the most sustainable locations, and
policies need to be justified. The evidence base is needed to
ensure that this can be demonstrated.
 
The successful contractor has
been selected through a competitive quotation from a selected pool
who have been involved in the development of similar work
previously. The Request for Quotation document (RFQ) was sent out
to five consultancies, four of which bid for the
contract.
 
 

No other options were
considered in relation to this critical piece of evidence. The WPVA
looks at the emerging Local Plan Review holistically and requires
up-to-date evidence to determine the impact policy requirements are
likely to have on the deliverability of development. This is a
specialist report and there are no resources to produce this
in-house.

Sanctuary Scheme funding, to fund React Property Maintenance Ltd to

content:
To
fund £34,038 of Sanctuary Scheme funding to survey properties
under Sanctuary Scheme and fit security measures. To enter into a
contract with React Property Maintenance Ltd to deliver the scheme
in Mansfield via a direct award with funding from the Domestic
Abuse grant up to the value of £34,038.
The
scheme will run from the 1st of April 2026 until the
31st March 2027.
To authorise the Legal Services
Manager to negotiate, finalise and complete all necessary legal
agreements and other documents to give effect to the
above.
 

The scheme is to
support survivors of domestic abuse in the Mansfield district by
fitting additional security measures in their properties to make
them feel safe in their homes. The Safe Accommodation funding terms
and conditions states it can be used for this purpose.
A contract
exemption form has been approved by the Assistant Director for
Housing due to the sensitivity of the scheme and the specialist
nature of the assessment process and vulnerable client group
benefitting from the scheme. The contract exemption also considers
the fact that the scheme is in high demand in Mansfield and
therefore essential to have capacity to continue the scheme
seamlessly, but is short term grant funding.
Under the contract procedure rules 3.12.76 of
the 
constitution, para d, the contract
award meets the procurement exemption due to the supply of goods or
services that are specialised and in the opinion of the appropriate
Assistant Director no reasonably satisfactory alternative is
available.
This is not a key
decision as the funding is below £50,000.
 

No alternative options
considered as company is a specialist and other local authorities
use them for their Sanctuary Scheme.
 
Not to provide the funding
– this would mean vulnerable people would be left without the
reassurance and security provided to them by the scheme.
topline: The Assistant Director of Housing has decided to approve funding for security measures in properties for survivors of domestic abuse in Mansfield district

purpose:
1.1 Attached at Appendix 1 is the attached
Audit Completion Report (ISA 260) summarises the conclusions of the
audit work carried out by Council’s External Auditors (Forvis
Mazars) on the Council’s Annual Statement of Accounts
2024/25. This report states an unqualified opinion on the financial
statements.

1.2 Attached at Appendix 2 is the Auditor’s Annual Report,
which gives more detail regarding the Value for Money work which
the auditors have completed.
content:
The external auditor presented a summary of
the Audit Completion Report to the Committee. The Committee was
informed that the Completion report set out the findings of the
audit for 2024/2025.
 
The auditor advised that he would present the
key findings of the audit to the Committee.
 
Members were informed that the auditor would
be giving an unqualified opinion on the Council financial
statements and that is that the accounts show a true and fair view
of the Councils financial position and that it has been properly
prepared in accordance with accounting standards.
The Committee was informed that there were
small number of findings in this report that start with section 5
and 6 of the report. Members were reminded that at previous
committee meetings that there had been an issue identified around
bank reconciliation, these have been brought up to date. But it has
been identified as significant control deficiency in our audit
findings, there were a small number of deficiencies that had also
been identified in appendix A.
 
In terms of changes to the accounts these were
outlined on section 6 of the report. There were a small number of
unadjusted errors these are unadjusted because these are not
material and therefore management had decided not to adjust the
errors, because these were based on our extrapolations as seen in
the description you will see the actual error identified which is a
much smaller amount. The auditor advised that there was a
requirement to extrapolate to ensure that this was not an
indication of a wider material error. The auditor advised that they
were satisfied that this was not the case and therefore they remain
an unadjusted misstatement in the accounts.
 
The auditor advised that there were also some
adjusted misstatements that started on page 23 of the report. The
auditor provided a summary of these to the Committee. These had
been corrected. The Committee was informed that there had been a
number of disclosure misstatements that were set out on page 25 of
the auditor report.
 
The auditor advised that the Value for Money
findings were set out in section 8 of the report, in which two
significant weaknesses were identified in the Council’s
arrangements the first one related to the Housing Repairs
Procurement which had been previously discussed in detail at
previous committee meetings, which had been identified through the
Corporate Assurance Manager’s team and the second was the
bank reconciliation which was a key control in the process and
should be kept up to date.
 
Councillor Hartshorn asked for guidance on the
errors identified and asked what that meant to the authority.
 
The auditor responded that in most cases it
does not impact on the Council’s bottom line, the identified
errors were classification error or technical errors that flow
through into the unusable reserves and had no impact on general
funding.
 
The Chair advised that the Financial Services
Manager and the Team had broken this down effectively so that the
Committee understood it.
 
The external auditor advised that he would be
happy to provide training for the Committee on the External
Auditors role if Members wanted it.
 
The Chair and Committee advised that this
would be much appreciated.
 
The external auditor advised that the other
report that was on the agenda was the Annual Auditors report and
that this was in effect a summarisation of the result of the audit
that was public facing and was on the Council’s website
alongside the Council's accounts. The auditor advised that the
appendix needed to be updated to include the significant risks but
that this would be completed. The external auditor advised that the
work was now complete. The Committee was informed that the report
also included the commentary on the Council’s value for money
arrangements.
 
Councillor Hartshorn proposed that the report
be noted, Council Hughes seconded the motion.
 
On putting the motion to the vote, it was
unanimously approved.
Resolved:
That the report be noted.

content:
The Assistant Director of Law and Governance
and People informed the Committee that the report proposed
amendments to the Constitution as supported by the Constitutional
Working Group.
 
The Assistant Director of Law and Governance
and People advised that the report provided the opportunity for the
Committee to consider the amendments and to comment and shape the
amendments that the Working Group had supported prior to
recommendation to the Mayor or Council for adoption.
 
The Assistant Director of Law and Governance
and People highlighted the significant amendments proposed to the
Constitution these included a change to the Key Decision thresholds
as at page 14 of the report at 4.4.  The
proposed amendments would be from the existing £50,000
revenue to £150,000 and the Capital threshold from
£250K to £300K.
 
The Committee was also informed that there
were proposed changes to:

a)     
the Contract Procedures rules so that they were in line with the
Procurement Act 2023 (page 16, paragraph 4.6),

b)    
amendments to the Planning Applications Committee Terms of
Reference (4.8.7),

c)     
  the Employee Code of Conduct
(4.12) as agreed with the unions provided that when adopted this is
promoted to staff,

d)    
the Code of Conduct for Councillors and Co-opted members with the
Adoption of the LGA Model Code which would bring this authority in
line with other authorities across Nottinghamshire and subject to
the inclusion of local provisions as set out in the report.

e)     
the rules of procedure for Council (as at 4.20 of the report) in
relation to the deadlines for Motions, and Public and Councillor
questions. it was proposed that the deadline for Councillor
questions to be moved to 12 noon on the day after the agenda is
published and the deadline for motions to be confirmed as 12 noon
on the day before the Council Agenda is published.
 
The Assistant Director for
Law and Governance and People, proposed an amendment to the
proposals set out in the report in relation to the Terms of
Reference for the Planning Applications Committee. Under point 1 in
Appendix B to the report, it was proposed that the bracketed words
“(excluding householder and minor commercial applications) be
removed  for
the purposes of clarity.
Andrea Smith queried how the threshold for Key
Decisions had been calculated and asked what the rationale was for
the amendment and queried if this was in line with other
authorities.
 
The Assistant Director of Law and Governance
and People informed the Committee that the amount varied widely
across the country and unitary and county councils have higher
thresholds than district authorities. The legislation requires that
councils consider their own budgets and as to what the appropriate
threshold would be. The Committee was informed that the threshold
proposed was in line with other authorities, and that the current
thresholds for the Key Decisions, particularly the revenue
threshold, were much less than other authorities as indicated in
the table at 4.4.4 of the report.
 
The Corporate Director for Resources/Deputy
CEO assured the Committee that the services that are delivered by
district authorities are all similar and therefore
Mansfield’s budgets are not significantly different from
other Districts.
 
Councillor Hartshorn referred to page 18
paragraph 4.8.8 of the report and asked for clarity on this
paragraph.
 
The Assistant Director of Law, Governance and
People responded that at the moment if
there is a Planning Application then any Member can request that it
is escalated to a Planning Applications Committee., The Working
Group felt would be appropriate that it was restricted to the Ward
Member or any Member representing any other affected
Ward.  Therefore, this has been updated
in the attached appendix B to the report.
 
The Committee confirmed they were supportive
of the proposed amendments as set out in the report and including
the additional amendment proposed at the meeting, and that these
should be recommended to the Mayor in respect of Executive
proposals and that non-Executive proposals and the required
Constitutional amendments be recommended to Council for
approval.
 
The Chair informed the Committee that the
recommendations to the Committee were, that the Committee review
the Executive amendments to the Constitution and provide feedback
to the Mayor, and that they review the Non-Executive amendments to
the Constitution and recommend this to Council for adoption.
 
Councillor Denness proposed the recommendation
and Councillor Moxon seconded the motion.
 
On putting the motion to the vote, it was
unanimously approved.
 
Resolved:
(i)            
That the Committee review the Executive amendments to the
Constitution and provide feedback to the Mayor;
(ii)          
That they review the Non-Executive amendments to the Constitution
and recommend this to Council for adoption
topline: The Assistant Director of Law and Governance has decided to propose amendments to the Constitution regarding key decision thresholds and codes of conduct, which were unanimously approved by the Committee.

summary of the key aspects of the Treasury Management Monitoring
Report 1 April 2025 to 31 December 2025 specifically around
borrowing and investing.
 
The Committee was informed that the report
provided an update on the Council’s Treasury activity and
Prudential Indicators during the period 1 April 2025 to 31 December
2025.
 
The Committee was referred to section 4.1 of
the report that indicated the Council’s new borrowing during
the period 1 April 2025 to 31 December 2025 was £20M in new
loans, as of 31 December 2025 the Council’s borrowing stood
at £70.8M. The Committee was informed that majority of the
debt was with the Public Loans Board that offers preferential rates
to local authorities and it was anticipated that during 2025/26, up
to £45m of new borrowing would be required.
 
The Financial Services Manager referred the
Committee to Section 5 of the report that discussed the
Council’s investments. Section 5.2 of the report confirmed
that the Council had a total of £16.5m invested as at 31
December 2025. The Committee was informed that all the
Council’s investments were within the agreed maximum limits
as set out in the Annual Treasury Management Strategy for
2025/2026. Investments were detailed at Table 4 of the report.
 
Members were referred to section 6 of the
report that indicated the Council’s rate of return, with an
average rate of return has decreased from 5.14% to 4.40% as the
result of the Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee reducing
the bank rate from 5.25% to 3.75% from July 2024 to December
2025.
 
The Committee was informed that the current
expectation was for the base rate to see further reductions during
2026/2027, reaching 3.25% by March 2027.
 
During quarter 3 of 2025/2026 the Council did
not invest with any financial institutions that fell below the
approved minimum level by Council when it set the Treasury
Management strategy in March 2025.
Andrea Smith Independent Member clarified that
the Council had always operated within the treasury limits and
prudential indicators as set out in paragraph 7.3 except for the
borrowing strategy described in paragraph 4.7 of the report.
 
The Financial Services Manager confirmed
this.
 
Councillor Hartshorn proposed that the
Treasury Management monitoring report 1 April 2025 to 31 December
2025 be noted, Councillor Denness seconded the motion. On putting
the motion to the vote this was unanimously approved.

That the Treasury Management monitoring report
1 April 2025 to 31 December 2025 be noted.

The Private

January 2025 from the Occupational Therapy team at Nottinghamshire
County Council requesting a disabled adaptation ref. DFG 2477. The
referral requested an extension with bedroom and bathroom/wet
room.

quote for the adaptation. All of the

Substantial time has been spent
working with the client and occupational therapist
to identify alternative access

purpose:
To seek approval to appoint a project manager
for the crematorium refurbishment project, following a procurement
process carried out by Nottinghamshire County Council
content:
Appointment of Crematorium
Refurbishment Project Manager
 
 
Approve the award of the Project Management contract for the
refurbishment of the crematorium., noting that the funding has been
approved by the Joint Crematorium Committee.
 
The Legal Services Manager be
authorised to negotiate, finalise and complete all necessary legal
agreements and other documents to give effect to the
above
 

 
Mansfield District Council
require a single supplier to act as an Employer’s Agent (EA)
and Project Manager to lead and coordinate the refurbishment of the
Mansfield & District Crematorium including the installation of
2 new electric cremators, following the approval of the capital
spend by the Joint Crematorium Committee.
 
Mansfield & District
Crematorium requires refurbishment as the current facility is now
outdated in terms of spatial organisation, accessibility, internal
environment, and aesthetic presentation. Furthermore, the
mechanical and electrical systems are end-of-life and the cremators
themselves no longer meet expected standards for operational
efficiency or environmental performance, especially due to the lack
of mercury abatement equipment.  In
response to these challenges, the Joint Crematorium Committee has
committed to a full refurbishment of the facility. The selected
pathway is an extensive refurbishment which entails a full
reconfiguration of the crematorium’s internal layout,
recladding of external elevations to enhance energy performance and
visual appearance and installation of two new electric
cremators.
 
Cremator installation is a
specialist service and requires a contractor with previous
experience in this field due to the operational environment and the
equipment to be installed.  On this
basis the quality questions, for submission by interested parties,
were heavily weighted towards the project manager’s previous
experience of managing similar projects, overseeing the
installation of cremation equipment and experience of managing a
refurbishment on a live sensitive site.
7 submissions were received
with 5 being proceedable.  The
recommended contractor met the minimum requirements for quality and
offered the lowest price of the bids eligible for contract award
making their bid the Most Advantageous Tender overall. Mansfield
District Council Design Services Team will act as critical friend
throughout the project, providing further scrutiny and reassurance
for members.

 
The project management of the
project was a consideration for all the authority areas however ADC
and NSDC do not have an internal Design Services team.  MDC Have insufficient capacity to be able to
manage the full project however will act as client.
topline: The Assistant Director - Neighbourhood Services has decided to appoint a Project Manager for the refurbishment of Mansfield & District Crematorium.

best value, including social value, and whether the framework
included existing contractors and local SMEs. It was determined
that this procurement event is in line with the contract procedure

facilitated by Nottinghamshire County Council to ensure we are
legally compliant with the current procurement rules and
legislation.

content:
To approve the transfer of the hosting of the
HR shared service from Mansfield District Council to Ashfield
District Council

HR Shared Service Delivery
Model
 
Delegated Decision Ref:
25/50/CEO

Reason for Decision:
 
The HR Shared Service is
responsible for:

HR provision
including review and application of policies, guidance, employee
relations, attendance management and
reviews/restructures
Payroll services for
employees, Elected Members and elections staff. Includes processing
pay, overtime, allowances, pensions, and statutory payments and
data returns to His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs (HMRC),
Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS), etc.
Management and
administration of individual employee files
Recruitment Portal
and services
Learning, Development
and Training programmes
Union Engagement and
Negotiation
Occupational Health
contracted service
Application of Job
Evaluation/Moderation
Application of Pay
& Grading Structure
Self-Service –
e.g., Time recording, leave management, etc.

 
The HR Shared Service is not
responsible for:

Approval of HR
policies.
Approval of Single
Status Agreements involving Employee Terms and
Conditions
Approval of
Collective Agreements with Trade Unions
Determination of Pay
& Grading Structures including salaries
Determination of Job
Evaluation Scheme
Level of
Organisational Risk Appetite
Staff
restructures
Employee Relations
Decisions e.g., dismissals on grounds of misconduct or
capability
 

Responsibility for the above
falls to Council, Cabinet and/or Head of Paid Service and managers
in accordance with the Council’s Constitution, Scheme of
Delegation and HR Policies.
 
Background to the Shared
Service
 
As part of the programme of
implementing shared services between ADC and MDC, the Shared HR
Service commenced on
1 December 2013 where it was agreed that MDC would host the
service. ADC-HR Service employees transferred to MDC. The
initial Service Level Agreement (SLA) was for a period of 5 years
with an option to review.
 
The key drivers for
implementing the shared service were primarily: increased staff
resilience, shared expertise and driving efficiencies (shared
systems, staff costs, pooled contract costs).
 
Prior to the end of the initial
5-year period, a review was undertaken that highlighted a high
level of achievements delivered through the HR Shared Service and
confirmation that the key drivers had been met with a saving to
both authorities of over 25% in efficiency costs. The continuation
of the HR Shared Service has and continues to maintain the best
value for money service delivery option for both ADC and
MDC.
 
Following a Corporate Peer
Review, ADC expressed an interest in hosting the HR Shared Services
in order to enable it to be developed to
better support its transformation programme. Under such an
arrangement, there will be no change to the HR services provided to
MDC under the Service Level Agreement. This decision therefore
enables ADC to achieve the ambitions they have for the service they
receive while not impacting on the cost or level of service to
MDC.
 
 
 
 

To continue with the shared
service and for MDC to continue to host.
 
To end the shared service
agreement and establish an HR service solely for MDC.
 
This is not the preferred model
for the reasons set out above.

purpose:
To endorse and approve the submission of the
final business case for local government reorganisation for the
area of Nottingham and Nottinghamshire, in line with government
requirements.
content:
Resolved by the Elected Mayor

 

i)                       
That the 1e Local Government Reorganisation business
case for Nottingham and Nottinghamshire, as set out in appendix D,
for submission to government as Mansfield District Council’s
final response to the Ministerial request for proposals for Local
Government Reorganisation. The details of 1e include the creation
of two unitary councils based on a north-south model. The first
based on the existing boundaries of Ashfield, Bassetlaw, Gedling,
Mansfield and Newark & Sherwood and the second based on
Broxtowe, Nottingham City and Rushcliffe.
ii)             
That delegated authority be given to the Chief
Executive Officer to make any final changes or amends to the
business case between now and the submission date of 28 November
2025 to government.
 

To ensure that council meets
the requirements of the statutory invitation from government it is
required to submit a final proposal for local government
reorganisation for the area of the county of Nottinghamshire by 28
November 2025.

(i)                 
The council can decide not to respond to the
Secretary of State’s invitation; however, a new structure
will be implemented irrespective of this. Notwithstanding concerns
about some aspects of reorganisation, the council has determined
that the responsible thing to do on behalf of the district is to
participate fully in the process. This includes making its position
known on a preferred option that reflects the criteria given for
reorganisation.
 
(ii)                
   Councils
could have developed proposals in isolation rather than
collectively across the whole area of the county of
Nottinghamshire. This would have risked options being developed
which meet the needs of part of the area but not the whole, and
which have less alignment with the criteria set out by MHCLG in the
statutory invitation. The proposed option for local government
reorganisation outlined in this report and detailed in Appendix D
have been developed through a structured and detailed work
programme overseen by leaders/mayors with support from chief
executives and advice and analysis from PWC and CIPFA. Although
support for differing options has emerged, this work has
continued.
topline: The Elected Mayor has decided to submit a business case for local government reorganisation in Nottingham and Nottinghamshire, proposing the creation of two unitary councils.

content:
The Financial Services Manager
presented an overview of the Treasury Management Monitoring report
for 1 April to 30 September 2025 report to the Committee. The
Committee was informed that the report was to provide an update on
the Treasury activity and prudential indicators during this
period
The Committee was advised that
the Treasury Management Strategy 2025/2026 was approved on 4 March
2025.
 
 The
report outlines how the Council performed against the approved
strategy up to the end of quarter 2.
 
The Committee was referred to
section 4.1 of the report which outlined the borrowing activities
of the Council. The Committee was advised that during the period
the Council took out borrowing of £20M of new loans and that
the Council’s borrowing was at £70.8M on 30 September
2025.  The Committee was informed that
the majority of the debt had been taken out with the Public Works
Loan Board as they offered preferential interest rates to local
authorities.
 
The Financial Services Manager
directed Members to section 5 – the Council’s
Investments throughout the year so far, and at section 5.2 as of 30
September 2025, the Council had £20.5M invested in financial
institutions.  The majority of the
investments being held with other local authorities a shown in
Table 3.
 
The Members were referred to
section 6 detailing the rate of return, which indicated the rate of
return against the investments… 
The Council received an average rate of return of 4.53% against the
average base rate of 4.21% for the period to 30 September 2025,
this was because of the Bank of England’s Monetary Policy
reducing the bank rate from 5.2% to 4% from July 2024 to 30 August
2025.
 
The Committee waws informed
that when investing money, the into Banks and Building Societies
that the Council does set high credit criteria so that this reduces
the risk of not getting its investments back due to default. During
the period until 30 September 2025, the Council did  not invest with any financial institutions that
fell below the minimum level approved by the Council Treasury
Management Strategy approved on 4 March 2025.
 
Andrea Smith Independent Member
asked if there was any relationship between the rate at which the
Council borrow and the rate at which the Council invests, and
queried if within the strategy there was an intention that states
that the Council will never borrow at a higher rate, than the
Council may get as a rate of return on investments, or if there was
no relation between the two financial decisions.
 
The Corporate Director/Deputy
Chief Executive Officer advised that it was dependant on as and
when the borrowing takes place and therefore dependant on what the
rates are, as generally when the Council needs to borrow it is for
large amounts that would be longer term, whereas investments are
often shorter term.  Therefore, the
Council would be looking at different things and would collaborate
closely with the Council brokers to get the best rates of
return.
 
The Independent Member
clarified that this was not linked therefore a strategic intention
to always maintain a net neutral approach to borrowing against net
return.
 
The Corporate Director/Deputy
Chief Executive Officer advised that this was not always
possible.
 
Councillor Hartshorn referred
to section 9.1 of the report  and asked
for clarification on the actions that had been implemented were to
help address the increased risk.
 
The Financial Services Manager
advised that the table following that on Risk Management was
responding to the risks indicated and actions taken.
The Chair informed the meeting
that the recommendation was that the Treasury Management Monitoring
report 1 April 2025 -30 September be noted and recommended to
Council in line with the CIPFA Code of Practice.
 
Councillor Hartshorn proposed
the recommendation; this was seconded by Councillor
Coxhead.
 
On putting the motion to the
vote, it was unanimously approved.
 
Resolved:
That the recommendation was
that the Treasury Management Monitoring report 1 April 2025 -30
September be noted and recommended to Council in line with the
CIPFA Code of Practice

to contain the improvements indicated by the Committee members who
attended the workshop.  Once drafted
this was taken to CLT who were happy with the strategy, and
following this another workshop was held as part of the procurement
workshop and reviewed it to see if Committee were satisfied with
the Internal Audit Strategy
 
The Corporate Assurance Manager
highlighted a few items within the three-year   strategy for the Committee.  The Committee was referred to page 94 which
indicated an Executive Summary, which listed the key strategic
objectives and the core values and principles that the Council are
committed to.
 
The Committee was referred to
section 6 – reviewing and reporting that the Committee was
informed would be a standalone CLT 
meeting in advance of reporting to the Committee, to look in detail
at the issues and how the risks are being managed.
 
The Committee was referred to
page 104 and informed that there had been a slight amendment to the
performance indicators. To be compliant with the Global Internal
Audit Standards and that there would be an internal review of the
delivery that would be reported to both CLT and the Committee
in regards to performance and whether
the Council is achieving its strategic 
operation objectives.
 
Andrea Smith –
Independent Member referred to a recommendation that was identified
last week relative to the Executive Summary on page 94, one of the
objectives is to lead on the Council’s counter fraud
arrangements to minimise risk.  The
independent Member wanted to reflect on that and stated that it was
not the Audits function to minimise risk, it is their function to
identify the risk and with the view that the accountable owners
would increment mitigating actions.  It
therefore potentially places the onus in the wrong place in terms
of risk management and therefore we recommend that the wording
should be amended to identifying.  
It is  very important that, that
statement is adjusted to reflect the role of the audit.  This was the recommendation that came out of that
group session.
 
The Chair stated that the
recommendation was that the Internal Audit Strategy for the period
2025-2026 at appendix 1 be approved.
 
Councillor Denness proposed the
recommendation, Councillor Hughes.  The
motion was carried by the Committee.
 
Resolved:
That the Internal Audit
Strategy for the period 2025-2026 at appendix 1 be
approved.
topline: The Governance & Standards Committee has decided to approve the Internal Audit Strategy for the period 2025-2026.

purpose:
To inform the committee of external audit's
progress to date.
content:
The Financial Services Manager
introduced Daniel Watson external auditor to the Committee to
present his report.
 
The external auditor informed
the Committee that the report was a progress report that set out
the details of the external audit completed so far.  The Committee was informed that it had been hoped
to be able to provide an Audit Completion report, however, there
had been some unforeseen delays due to illness of staff at
Mazars.  However, the Audit Completion
report was expected to be provided at the next meeting and would
therefore hit the February 2026 deadline.
 
The Committee was referred to
page 30 of the report that indicated the areas that the external
auditors were still working on, however all the information
required had now been received  for
those.
 
The Committee was informed that
the most significant area that was being worked on was related to
the Walkden Street Car Park and the lease related to that because
this had occurred after the year end and might impact on the
valuation within the accounts.  A
meeting had taken place yesterday regarding this and the required
information was received, and this was now being reviewed by Mazars
technical team.
 
The Committee was advised that
the other area that needed to be brought to the Members attention
was in terms of the findings on the control recommendations on page
33 which was related to the Council Bank Reconciliation which was
not up to date as at the year end.  This
was received in November and had now been brought up to date for
the year end and this was still being worked on for 2025-2026, this
would be brought up to date. 
This, had prevented the auditors from
completing areas like cash in the year until the reconciliation had
taken place.
 
The external auditor advised
that there would be a fuller picture on misstatements in the Audit
Completion report.
 
The Committee was informed that
the works on value for money was substantially complete , two
significant risks had been identified in the Council’s
arrangement one in relation to Internal Audits Report on Housing
Repairs Procurement that this Committee had already received and
the other was in relation to financial controls around the bank
reconciliation.  The Committee was
informed that the external auditors went through internal
consistency  processes with any risks of
significant weakness and this meeting would take place Monday 24
September 2025 any findings from that meeting would be agreed with
management and recorded at  the end of
November, and would be brought to the
next meeting for Members information.
 
Councillor Denness asked for
clarification of the impact of the Walkden Street car park as a
risk.
 
The external auditor advised
that because the collapse happened after the year end, the Council
needed to assess whether that impacted on the valuation in the
accounts and as this happened after the year end the accounts would
need to include any disclosures in the Council’s accounts as
to include impacts on the lease liability and the right of use
asset side of the calculation
 
Councillor Hartshorn referred
to page 30 of the report Status of Audit and commented that within
the text it had commented several times “about impact on
resources and that additional resources had, had to be
allocated”, the Member queried if this had impacted on any
additional costs to the authority.
 
The external auditor advised
that in some cases it would be related to delays that could have
been prevented, and this would be discussed with management, and a
fee would be agreed in those cases. 
However, if the delays were unavoidable then an overall view of the
audit would take place, and it would be worked out if any
additional fees would be chargeable for the delays.  It was commented that next year it would be
discussed as to how this could be managed more effectively to take
in account of leave etc.
 
Andrea Smith –
Independent Member followed on from the Members question to add
that  as a recommendation it was
important that individuals be made aware of the consequences of
information being misaligned or co-ordinated, notwithstanding
extenuating circumstances as it not only delayed the completion of
the report but it could also impact on
the costs to the Council.
 
The Chair looked forward to
receiving the update on this at the next meeting.
 
The Chair informed the meeting
that the recommendation was that the External Audit Progress report
be noted.
 
Councillor Denness proposed the
motion, this was seconded by Councillor Hartshorn.
 
On putting the motion to the
vote, it was unanimously approved.
 
Resolved:
That the External Audit report
be noted.

purpose:
Award of Contract for Analyse LOCAL systems
and services
content:
Contract Award -
Analyse Local
 
That the Director
of Corporate Resources/Deputy CEO authorise the awarding of a
renewal contract for a period of one year, with the option to
extend for a further year and at the cost as set out in the body of
the decision, to its existing supplier, Inform Holdings Ltd.
(formerly Inform CPI Ltd.) for continuing provision to the Revenues
and Benefits Service of Analyse Local products.
To authorise the
Legal Services Manager to negotiate, finalise and complete all
necessary legal agreements and other documents to give effect to
the above.
 

The Council is responsible for accurately
reporting, budgeting and maximisation of income from Business
Rates.  The areas of work relating
directly to the awarding of the contract are:
·       
Identification of new and material changes to
hereditaments which can be reported to the Valuation Office to be
added to the rating list (Product: RV Finder), thereby increasing
collectible rates and income to the Council.
·       
Detection and correction of incorrectly claimed
Small Business Rates Relief (Product: SBRR Audit)
·       
Forecasting income from the Business Rates scheme as
part of the Council’s budget preparations (Product: Analyse
Local forecasting). 
Inform CPI Ltd, who were subsequently acquired
by Inform Holdings Ltd have been in successive contracts with the
Council’s Revenues and Benefits Service since 2019 for
provision of services referred to above (RV Finder, Analyse Local
Forecasting & SBRR Audit).  The most
recent contract expired on 19 October 2025.
The existing supplier has provided a
consistent level of service and performance by the supplier under
the existing contract in terms of data quality for forecasting and
relief monitoring and net additional business rates retained income
over the 2024 – 2025 contract term of
£138,000. 
The previous contract which ended on 19
October 2025 cost £8,500 per annum.  There has been an acceptable level of increase to
the cost of the renewal contract which is now £9,600 per
annum (exclusive of VAT) on the basis of a 1-year contract, with
the option to extend for a further 1 year.  Should the Council take up the extension, the
total across the two years would be £19,200. 
Due to the bespoke and specialist nature of
the service provided by the supplier, a contracts exception form
(No.49) has been completed in accordance with s 27.1 (c) of the
Councils’ contract procedure rules which was approved on 16
October 2025, a copy of which is shown as Appendix 1.

The Council has neither the
technical ability nor staffing resources to gather the data
supplied by the services offered by the supplier.  The suppliers’ services are specialist, and
no viable alternatives have been established on previous
comparisons.
 
With the Governments’
imminent reset of the Business Rates system, it is imperative that
the Council has continuity of service provision in this
area.
topline: The Director of Corporate Resources/Deputy CEO has decided to award a renewal contract for Analyse Local products to Inform Holdings Ltd.

purpose:
To seek approval from the Chief Executive/Head
of Paid Service to extend the temporary contract of the Marketing
and Communications Officer for the Destination Mansfield project
until the end of March 2026. This extension is required to ensure
delivery of key project outputs and to meet government funding
expectations, including campaigns, website development, signage,
and ambassador engagement, while options for longer-term
sustainable delivery models are explored. The cost of the extension
will be met in full from in-year savings within the Communications
budget.
content:
Extension of
Marketing and Communications Officer Post – Destination
 
Delegated Decision Ref:
25/36/CEO
 
 
To
approve, under delegated powers of the Chief Executive/Head of Paid
Service, the extension of the current temporary Marketing and
Communications Officer post (T000525) for a period of four months
(November 2025 – March 2026) at a cost of £10,352,
funded from in-year savings within the Communications
budget.
 
 

Reason for Decision:
 
Destination Mansfield is a
£500k funded project designed to raise the profile of
Mansfield as a place to live, work, visit and invest. The project
is at a critical stage with government-funded outputs and
expectations still to be delivered before the programme concludes
in 2025/26.
Key deliverables outstanding
include:

Finalisation of the
Destination Mansfield website design.
Delivery of new
welcome signage.
Three major
campaigns: Investment, Young People, and Mansfield
Ambassadors.
Ongoing development
of the Mansfield Ambassador scheme (currently 40+ members
engaged).
Exploration of
sustainable delivery models, including a potential Community
Interest Company (CIC) and alignment with the forthcoming Plan for
Neighbourhoods funding package.

The extension will ensure
continuity in delivery, protect progress already achieved, and
allow the Council to meet government expectations on outputs
associated with the funding.
Corporate Leadership Team has
agreed in principle that the post can be extended provided
sufficient in-year savings are available to fund the cost. These
savings have been identified and approved by the Deputy Chief
Executive.

Financial Implications:

The cost of extending the post for four months (November 2025
– March 2026) is £10,352 (Scale 4.3, based on 2025
payroll figures). This will be met from existing in-year savings
within the Communications budget as follows:

Saving on Communications Team Leader
post (August) – £3,559
Saving on Research and Insight
Officer (budgeted at 5.4, paid at 4.2) – £2,211
Saving on Communications Officer
(2-month vacancy, May–June 2025) – £5,442

Total Savings Identified: £11,212
Total Cost of Extension: £10,352
Balance Remaining: £860

No additional funding is required.
 
 
 

Do nothing: Allow the contract to end in
November 2025. This would result in the loss of delivery capacity,
a gap in support for critical campaigns, and an increased risk of
not meeting the required outputs of the Destination Mansfield
project.

Seek alternative external funding immediately: Attempts to secure
continuation funding through the Long Term Plan for Towns and UKSPF
were unsuccessful. While Plan for Neighbourhoods funding may
provide longer-term support, this will not be available until April
2026, leaving a six-month delivery gap.
 
Failure to extend the role
would risk delivery of government-funded outputs and the momentum
already achieved through Destination Mansfield. This could
negatively impact the Council’s reputation with partners,
funders, and the local community. Extending the post supports the
Council’s commitment to raising the profile of Mansfield as a
place to live, work, visit, and invest.
topline: The Chief Executive Officer has decided to approve the extension of the Marketing and Communications Officer post for four months to ensure the successful delivery of key projects under the Destination Mansfield initiative.

decision_maker: Portfolio Holder for Regeneration and Growth
purpose:
This report seeks approval to extend the
Mansfield Townscape Heritage Programme by seven months, to 31 July
2026, and to expand the eligible area of the programme to include
the Old Town Hall
content:
Resolved by the Elected Mayor on behalf of the
Portfolio Holder for Regeneration and Growth.
(i)
To approve a formal extension from the National Lottery Heritage
Fund
(NLHF), for the Mansfield THP until the end of July 2026 and to
agree the
implications thereof, notably:
• The
consideration of a grant application to restore and enhance the
rear wall
and
the 2 shopfronts (Units 1-2 Queen’s Walk) to side / exterior
of the Old
Town Hall.
• The appointment
of Design Services to act as the client project manager,
who
will also seek to appoint conservation architects to support the
project given
its
specialist restoration and conservation requirements.
• The extension
of the contract for the community participation co-ordinator
to
the
end of the programme.
• The
reappointment of the evaluation consultant to undertake and
complete
the
programme evaluation.
(ii) To approve the NLHF an extension of the area covered by
the
Mansfield THP, to include the Old Town Hall. This would be on
the basis that the
remaining capital and revenue budgets will be allocated to the
restoration of the
rear wall facing Millennium Gardens and the two shopfronts at
Units 1 and 2,
Queen’s Walk.
(iii) To approve an amendment to the capital and revenue budgets
of the Townscape
Heritage Programme to reflect the changes because of this
decision
and
as set out in paragraphs 4.9-4.11.
(iv) The Legal Services Manager
be authorised to negotiate, finalise and complete all.

(i)
To allow the THP to continue and facilitate investment of the
remaining
capital funds on projects of heritage significance, that do not
rely on private
sector match-funding and that can be delivered within agreed
timeframes and
remaining THP budget, further enhancing the conservation
area.
(ii) To allow for the heritage activities programme to continue
and deliver high
quality participatory and cultural outcomes resulting in an
enhanced
awareness of heritage across the town.
(iii) To continue with the
momentum created by the recommencement of the THP programme post
pandemic, facilitated by the remaining THP budgets.

Other options considered but rejected.
(i): Do nothing/ Conclude the THP by 31.12.2025 – The
Council may
decide not to expand the eligible programme area to include the
Old Town
Hall and consequently, not to extend the Mansfield TH programme
to 31 July
2026.
(ii) However, this decision will result in the NLHF withdrawing
its offer in principle
to
extend the TH grants programme to include the Old Town
Hall.
Consequently, the THP would end on 31 December 2025, with
over
£200,000 of TH funding being returned to the NLHF and
£90,000 of UK
Shared Prosperity Fund (UKSPF)
funding being returned to the East Midlands Combined County
Authority (EMCCA).
topline: The Portfolio Holder for Regeneration and Growth has decided to approve an extension from the National Lottery Heritage Fund for the Mansfield THP, allowing for restoration projects at the Old Town Hall and continuation of heritage activities.

purpose:
To enter into an associated lease agreement
with North Notts Hockey Club for the lease of Manor astro turf
pitch
content:
Subject to advertising the disposal and considering any
objections, to lease the astroturf pitch at Manor Sports Complex to
North Notts Hockey Club for 25 years at £1000 pa (except in
the first year when the cost will be nil subject to the club
carrying out specified improvement works) and subject to such other
terms as the Corporate Asset Manager considers
necessary.
 
The Legal Services Manager be
authorised to negotiate, finalise and complete all necessary legal
agreements and other documents to give effect to the
above

The council had been in negotiation with
Manor School to bring community access back to the astroturf pitch
on the site, which has been closed by the school since 2019. This
concluded with the relinquishment of the lease (between the council
and the school/ Two Counties Trust). The lease with the school has
now come to an end and a new lease transfer/ agreement of the pitch
to North Notts Hockey Club is now required.
 
The hockey club have undertaken significant work to the pitch to bring it back to a playable
standard, following years of no use. The council are happy to
support the club with a small contribution via a free first year
lease charge to the club.
 
After the first year the agreed annual
lease fees will be charged at £1k per year.  It is hoped that this support will allow the club
to establish themselves onto the pitch once again and undertake all
necessary work to bring it to a playable standard.
 
 

To not lease the
pitch and it remains closed to community use with the risk of it
falling into disrepair
topline: The Assistant Director - Neighbourhood Services has decided to lease the astroturf pitch at Manor Sports Complex to North Notts Hockey Club for 25 years, with the first year being free for specified improvement works.
